What number is missing from the division problem above?" :question/worked-solution "We have $\frac{5}{8}$ on the left and $\frac{5}{24}$ on the right.

![](images/67/67dd516958b830c5442ab740683b23866c09e9422ac48c9259131f73870ae951.png)

The division operation splits each vertical line into $3$ equal parts. So the shaded parts on the left are $3$ times larger than the shaded parts on the right.  

Therefore, the division problem shown is

$$

- split the fraction into ${\color{red}{2}}$ equal parts, and

- determine the fraction that makes up each part.

For example, suppose we wish to find the value of 

$$
\dfrac{4}{5} \div 2.
$$

Let's start by drawing the fraction model for $\dfrac45\mathbin{:}$

![](images/d1/d159ff7e61ae308f27dd561cc8b219f0fc5b5fa46135ebff70ed15558186280b.png)

We need to divide this fraction by ${\color{red}{2}}.$ To do this, we draw a horizontal line through our fraction that splits it into $\color{red}2$ *equal parts*.

![](images/87/87c0a9dad9ab63de7858e8857e412b4d6ce849dfc0b02a172a5debe420c5baf6.png)

We only need to determine the fraction that makes up one of the parts. Therefore, we can focus on only one row (i.e., the bottom row).

Now, we remove all the shaded parts not in the bottom row. 

![](images/54/54a3760d69e7622afa800e4fe107cdafc7069a1fd31138a9ad6c63e8cf6f8f1f.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\dfrac{4}{10}$ of the whole. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{4}{5} \div 2 = \dfrac{4}{10} \, .
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186143062 :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$

[{:db/id 17592186143890 :step/content {:db/id 17592186144002 :tutorial/content "When we divide a fraction by a whole number, say ${\color{red}{2}}$, the idea is to

- split the fraction into ${\color{red}{2}}$ equal parts, and
- determine the fraction that makes up each part.

For example, suppose we wish to find the value of

$$
\dfrac{4}{5} \div 2
$$

Let's start by drawing the fraction model for

$$
\dfrac45
$$

![](images/d1/d159ff7e61ae308f27dd561cc8b219f0fc5b5fa46135ebff70ed15558186280b.png)

We need to divide this fraction by ${\color{red}{2}}$. To do this, we draw a horizontal line through our fraction that splits it into $\color{red}2$ *equal parts*.

![](images/87/87c0a9dad9ab63de7858e8857e412b4d6ce849dfc0b02a172a5debe420c5baf6.png)

We only need to determine the fraction that makes up one of the parts. Therefore, we can focus on only one row (i.e., the bottom row).

Now, we remove all the shaded parts not in the bottom row.

![](images/54/54a3760d69e7622afa800e4fe107cdafc7069a1fd31138a9ad6c63e8cf6f8f1f.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents

$$
\dfrac{4}{10}
$$

of the whole. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{4}{5} \div 2 = \dfrac{4}{10} \,
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "411e9b60-5c7b-58a3-ba5a-8abc08a8f51a" :tutorial/math-academy-id 2029 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "467f66f4-545a-520d-bca9-01a2adeee469" :step/math-academy-id
